claims.statement: The pinned session fragment distinguishes default account syncing, whose web/mobile views are read-only, from remote control, which must be enabled to steer. Synced visibility does not prove remote execution continuity, steering authority or an active session; no remote control was enabled.

The non-Auto cloud-agent list resolves at the pin to Claude Opus 4.7/5/5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Haiku 4.5; Gemini Flash 3.5/3.6/3.7/3.8; GPT-5.4 mini, GPT-5.6 Luna/Sol/Terra, GPT-6 Astra/Luna/Sol, GPT-6.1 Sol; Grok 4.5/4.6/4.7 and MAI-Code-1.1-Flash. It is an enumerated fragment, not live entitlement or a complete all-mode inventory.

The agent-mode description delegates file and step selection, proposes edits and terminal commands and iterates toward the original task, with complex multi-step tasks and external integrations as suggested use cases. Intended completion is not a guarantee or authorization to execute arbitrary external tools.
The agent-mode billing fragment states each entered prompt consumes AI credits. No exact rate, available budget or approval to spend follows from that source statement; no prompts were submitted.

The edit-mode fragment limits availability to VS Code and JetBrains and distinguishes user-chosen files, per-iteration context and post-turn edit acceptance from autonomous agent selection. Proposed edits remain unaccepted until a decision; this description does not prove a sandbox restricting every possible operation.
The edit-mode recommendations favor defined-file updates and control of request count. User control is a capability claim, not measured token expenditure or assurance of cost-free operation.

The extension fragment describes marketplace installation or private organization development and selection via an at-sign list or full slug before a prompt. External-tool context is a trust/data boundary; list presence does not establish safe implementation, current support, authorization or execution.
